title: The Unity of Scripture
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: The unity of Scripture means that the Bible speaks as one coherent testimony to God’s character, works, promises, judgments, redemption, and glory. Though written through many human authors, Scripture reveals one unfolding purpose centered in Christ.
summary: The unity of Scripture means that the Bible speaks as one coherent testimony to God’s character, works, promises, judgments, redemption, and glory. Though written through many human authors, Scripture reveals one unfolding purpose centered in Christ.
christFocus: Jesus taught that the Scriptures bear witness to Him. The unity of Scripture is seen most clearly as the whole Bible points toward Christ, is fulfilled in Christ, and leads God’s people to worship and follow Him.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
The Bible contains many books, genres, authors, settings, covenants, commands, promises, warnings, and stories, but it is not a scattered collection of disconnected religious material. God speaks through the whole of Scripture with one redemptive purpose.

The unity of Scripture does not erase the real differences between law, history, wisdom, prophecy, Gospel, epistle, and apocalyptic writing. Each part must be read carefully according to its context. Yet all Scripture belongs within God’s larger work of creation, fall, promise, redemption, restoration, and glory.

Christ is central to this unity. The Scriptures testify to Him through promise, pattern, prophecy, fulfillment, sacrifice, kingdom, wisdom, priesthood, and hope. The Bible does not merely give moral lessons; it reveals God’s saving work.

This doctrine helps believers read the whole Bible with confidence. Difficult passages, unfamiliar books, and Old Testament promises are not isolated fragments. They belong to the one story of God’s faithful purpose fulfilled in Christ.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Without the unity of Scripture, people may misuse the Bible as disconnected quotes, moral examples, or private inspiration detached from God’s redemptive plan. They may focus on favorite passages while ignoring the larger message.

This doctrine helps believers see the faithfulness of God across time. The same God who speaks in Genesis, the Psalms, the prophets, the Gospels, and the apostles is revealing His glory and saving purpose through one united Word.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Read the Bible as one unified Word from God. Do not isolate passages from their place in Scripture’s whole message. Ask how each passage reveals God, exposes sin, points toward Christ, forms faith, and calls for obedience. Let the unity of Scripture deepen your confidence in God’s faithfulness.
